title: Super source follower
description: A super source follower (SSF): a plain source follower whose output resistance is driven down by a local feedback device. The input follower sets the DC level shift (the output sits about one input $V_{GS}$ below the input), and the feedback device senses the follower current and closes a local loop that lowers the output resistance by the loop gain $g_{m,fb}/g_{ds,in}$ (the feedback transconductance into the follower's own output resistance): $R_{out} \approx g_{ds,in}/((g_{m,in} + g_{mb,in}) * g_{m,fb})$, versus $1/g_{m,in}$ for a plain follower. The input device's source is the output, the feedback device sits between the output and ground, and the feedback device's gate is the input device's drain. So the input device's drain-source voltage is not a free choice — it is the feedback device's gate-source voltage minus the output level. Two currents are typed, one per source: the bias source into the input device's drain sets $I_{in}$, which the input device carries down to the output, and the output source, an ideal current from the supply into the output node worth $I_{fb} - I_{in}$, adds the rest, so the feedback device carries $I_{fb}$ to ground. That output source is what makes this a super source follower rather than a flipped voltage follower: it lets the feedback device run at its own current, and with it its own $g_m$, while the input device's current stays fixed. Both sources are ideal: each stands for the bias device a realization places there, typically a current-source transistor on a bias line, which this sheet does not size. That makes it a compact low-impedance buffer. The feedback is a local loop; its own phase margin (whether that loop is stable) is a small-signal AC check the simulator owns, out of this sheet's scope — this sheet sizes the DC operating point and the low-frequency output resistance only. The input gate is held at the output level plus the input device's $V_{GS}$, the input level the application presents, so no gate is a port. The output level, vds_fb, is stated at the design point and carries a hold: where the design is held at another condition, the input gate stays at that level and the output is solved again under it. On the demo NMOS table both devices size against the same data.

params.name: I_in
params.note: the bias source's current into the input device's drain: the input follower carries it, held fixed, which linearizes the buffer

params.name: I_fb
params.note: the feedback device's current: what the input device brings down to the output plus what the output source adds, so the output source is worth I_fb - I_in. At I_fb = I_in that source carries nothing and the cell is a flipped voltage follower

params.name: gm_id_fb
params.note: feedback device inversion: at fixed I_fb it sets gm_fb, and with it the loop gain gm_fb/gds_in

params.name: L_fb
params.note: the loop gain gm_fb/gds_in does not depend on L_fb (gm_fb is set by gm_id_fb and I_fb), so this knob moves the feedback device's vdsat and area, not Rout

params.name: vds_fb
params.note: feedback-device drain-source, which is the output node: the feedback device sits between the output and ground. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed, the input device's gate (this node plus its gate-source voltage) is what stays put and the node is solved again under it, between min and max.

doc.title: Feedback device
doc.description: The local-feedback device that senses the follower current; its transconductance into the follower's output resistance, gm_fb/gds_in, is the loop gain that lowers the output resistance. It sinks everything that arrives at the output node: the input device's current plus the output source's.

doc.title: Input follower device
doc.description: The source-follower input device carrying a fixed current; its gm sets the base output resistance and its vgs the DC level shift.

equations.name: vds_in
equations.note: input-device drain-source: its drain sits on the feedback device's gate, one feedback gate-source voltage above ground, and its source is the output

equations.name: gm_in
equations.note: input follower transconductance (sets the plain-follower output resistance 1/gm_in)

equations.name: av0_fb
equations.note: reference reading of the feedback device's own intrinsic gain; the loop gain that Rout actually divides by is gm_fb/gds_in, not this

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: SSF output resistance: the local loop drives the follower's own output conductance down by the product of the two transconductances. The gds is the INPUT device's — it is the input device whose drain current the loop senses — and the source-body generator adds to gm because the output node is the input device's source. On a sky130 tt realization of this buffer this form lands within 3% of the measured 56 ohm

equations.name: Rout_plain
equations.note: the plain source-follower output resistance, for comparison

equations.name: level_shift
equations.note: output sits about one input Vgs below the input (source-follower DC level shift)

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents, taken as the input device's whole gate capacitance. It OVERSTATES what a driver sees — the source follows the gate near unity, bootstrapping most of the gate-source capacitance away. No check reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the two sources drawn: the bias source's I_in into the input device and the output source's I_fb - I_in into the output, which together are what the feedback device sinks. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

checks.note: the buffer output resistance meets the target
